stem: Meena, a student in Jaipur, has a sore throat and mild fever. Her doctor checks her and says it is a viral cold, so no antibiotic is needed. Later, her uncle takes leftover antibiotic tablets whenever he feels slightly unwell. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Antibiotics are suitable for every infection, so Meena should take them for her cold.
Antibiotics kill bacteria, but careless use lets resistant bacteria develop, so the same antibiotic becomes less effective.
Careless antibiotic use makes bacteria easier to kill, so the same antibiotic becomes more effective.
A fever alone means an antibiotic is needed, so Meena must start antibiotics immediately.

teacher.key_rationale: Antibiotics act on bacteria, not viruses, so they are unsuitable for Meena's viral cold. Indiscriminate use selects for antibiotic-resistant bacteria, making future bacterial infections harder to treat. Only B states both ideas correctly; A is the every-infection trap, C reverses the resistance relationship, D treats fever alone as the trigger.
